newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish labour min concerned about pension reform.
newsitem.headline: Polish labour min concerned about pension reform.

text.p: Poland's Labour Minister Tadeusz Zielinski said on Monday he was concerned that party bickering ahead of autumn's parliamentary elections may hamper the crucial reform of the country's social security system.
"My January appeal to politicians to work on the social security reform above any political divisions met dead silence," he told a news conference.
He said that despite the apparent lack of a braod political agreement on the reform the labour ministry would continue work on the project.

Zielinski said a special inter-ministry council was finishing work on two bills necessary for the reform but said it was difficult to say when they would be discussed by the whole government and submited to parliament.
The bills would pave the way for the creation of new privately managed pension funds endowing them with shares of firms undergoing privatisation.
The funds would take part of the burden of providing social security pay-outs from the heavily subsidised and inefficient state-owned Social Security Office (ZUS).

Analysts say several politicians in the ruling leftist coalition of ex-communists and a peasant party feared the launch of the reform in an election year would cost them votes of those who would lose out on the changes.
The overhaul would most likely cut state subsidy to farmers' pensions and roll back privileges of some groups such as miners or the military, they say.
The previous labour minister Andrzej Baczkowski, who died last November, promised to send the two bills to parliament by the end of March.
